messages.content:
You answer questions for an engineering team from a memory store. The user message holds the memory you may use, then the question.
Rules:
- Answer only from the memory provided. Do not use outside knowledge and do not guess.
- If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: I don't know
- When the memory does contain it, reply in one short line with just the value asked for (a name, a team, a service, a date, a note label, a reason) and nothing else.
- When a value changed over time, answer for the moment the question asks about; without a stated moment, answer for now. Today is 2026-06-30.
- Memory entries carry the date they were recorded. Treat a later entry as superseding an earlier one on the same subject.

Memory:
- As of 2026-04-13, the Ember team still owns the reporting service. [valid 2026-04-13 to now; recorded by standup/ember/2026-04-13-2]
- On 2026-04-08 the Atlas team noticed that webhooks' request volume halved following the client rollout and flagged it because it is not their service. [valid 2026-04-08 to now; recorded by standup/atlas/2026-04-08]
- Webhooks will require an idempotency key on every delivery, because duplicate deliveries in INC-2026-003 came from retries without one. [decision; valid 2026-02-26 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- During incident INC-2026-003, the webhooks service delivered some events twice on 2026-02-20. [valid 2026-02-26 to now; recorded by incident-review/INC-2026-003]
- On 2025-11-03 the Boreal team decided that webhooks will sign payloads with rotating keys, because a partner asked for key rotation in their security review. [decision; valid 2025-11-03 to now; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-11-03]
- On 2025-05-14 the Cinder team observed that webhooks' memory use grew steadily for a week after the cache change. [valid 2025-05-14 to now; recorded by standup/cinder/2025-05-14]
- As of 2025-11-24, the Atlas team owns the bus, having taken it over from the Boreal team. [valid 2025-11-24 to now; recorded by handover/2025-11-24-event-bus]
    earlier: As of 2025-08-15, the Boreal team still owns the bus. [valid 2025-08-15 to 2025-11-24; recorded by standup/boreal/2025-08-15-2]
- The feature-flags service was owned by the Ember team as of 2025-11-06, having moved from the Atlas team, until ownership transferred to the Atlas team on 2026-02-11. [decision; valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction]
    earlier: The feature-flags service was owned by the Ember team as of 2025-11-06, having moved from the Atlas team, until ownership transferred to the Dune team on 2026-02-11. [decision; valid 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-09; recorded by handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags]
    earlier: As of 2025-11-06, the feature-flags service is owned by the Ember team, having moved from the Atlas team. [decision; valid 2025-11-06 to 2026-02-11; recorded by handover/2025-11-06-feature-flags]
- The billing API was owned by the Atlas team from 2025-06-09, having moved from the Ember team, until ownership transferred to the Ember team on 2026-01-12. [decision; valid 2026-01-12 to now; recorded by handover/2026-01-12-billing-api]
    earlier: The billing API is owned by the Atlas team as of 2025-06-09, having moved from the Ember team; the Boreal team was recorded by mistake and never held it. [valid 2025-07-03 to 2026-01-12; recorded by handover/2025-07-03-billing-api-correction]

    earlier: The billing API is owned by the Atlas team. [valid 2025-01-08 to 2025-03-07; recorded by standup/atlas/2025-01-08-2]
- As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Atlas team, having moved from the Ember team; the Dune team never owned it. [decision; valid 2026-03-09 to now; recorded by handover/2026-03-09-feature-flags-correction]
    earlier: As of 2026-02-11, the feature-flags service is owned by the Dune team, having moved from the Ember team. [decision; valid 2026-02-11 to 2026-03-09; recorded by handover/2026-02-11-feature-flags]

Question: Who owns webhooks today?

message.reasoning:
The question asks who owns webhooks today (2026-06-30). Looking through the memory, I see entries about webhooks: request volume halved (Atlas noticed), idempotency key decision, duplicate deliveries, signing payloads with rotating keys (Boreal decided), memory use growth (Cinder observed). But none of these state ownership of the webhooks service. The Atlas team "flagged it because it is not their service" — that tells us Atlas doesn't own it, but doesn't say who does.

So the answer is: I don't know.
